text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All sanctions have been lifted against Belgrade and so-called outer wall of sanctions is "a fabricated term", says Yugoslav foreign minister Milan Milutinovic.

- Serbian Chamber of Commerce president Vlajko Stojiljkovic says substantial production and export growth expected soon, reduction of trade deficit and return to markets in neighbouring countries a priority.
- Serbian industry minister Oskar Fodor says barter arrangements with Russia and China will cut illegal oil imports, socially-owned property in Serbia will not be distributed for free to anybody.
- Heavy industry has no prospects, says head of the Serbian institute for development.
- Yugoslav customs officials discover 190 kilograms of heroin hidden among 20 tonnes of peppers in a Slovenian truck at Yugoslav-Bulgarian border.

- Talks between international mediator for succession of former Yugoslavia Sir Arthur Watts and expert teams of all former Yugoslav republics open in Brussels. No agreement yet on definition of state property subject to division.

- Poll conducted by Mark Plan agency among 2,500 people shows 23.7 percent would vote for Socialist Party, Yugoslav United Left and New Democracy coalition, 23.9 for Zajedno (Together) opposition coalition, while 29.7 are undecided.
- National Bank of Yugoslavia announces increase in reserve requirement for banks, despite bankers' complaints the central bank measures are blocking their activities.

- Bad structure of economy, poor quality and high prices of goods and services, and not just strikes, pose risks for foreign investors, says Dragan Radulovic, head of association of trade unions of Yugoslavia.
- First promotion of Belgrade-Sarajevo bus route today. Regular traffic between the two cities to open from Thursday.
- Charges to be raised soon in the Hague against members of Croatian army and civilian authorities for crimes in formerly Serb-held region of Krajina, according to Serb Krajina documentation centre.
- Eyewitness testimony to crimes against Croats from Vukovar by former Yugoslav military police reservist: "We were powerless to prevent the horror". -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
